title: Randomized and controlled clinical trial of the efficacy and safety of the use of lidocaine and magnesium sulfate for lung resection surgery using Video-Assisted Thoracic Surgery (VATS)
official: Randomized and controlled clinical trial of the efficacy and safety of the use of lidocaine and magnesium sulfate for lung resection surgery using Video-Assisted Thoracic Surgery (VATS)
summary: Main objective: To analyze whether the intravenous administration of lidocaine and magnesium sulfate during the intraoperative period of patients with lung resection using VATS reduces morphine consumption in the first 24 postoperative hours.
conditions: Lung resection surgery using Video-Assisted Thoracic Surgery (VATS)

interventions.name: Suero fisiológico 0,9% Baxter (Clear Flex) solución para perfusión
Lidocaína B. Braun 20 mg/ml solución inyectable
Sulfato de Magnesio Altan 150 mg/ml solución inyectable y para perfusión EFG

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients undergoing lung tumor resection surgery using video-assisted thoracoscopy.
2. The patient must be 18 years of age or older.
3. The patient, or his or her representative, has given consent to participate in the study.
4. The patient must, in the opinion of the investigator, be able to comply with all the requirements of the clinical trial.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patients who have previously been diagnosed with chronic pain prior to surgery.
2. Patients unable to clearly understand the objectives and methodology of the study.
3. Patients with chronic kidney damage with glomerular filtration < 60 ml/min (stage III-V).
4. Patients with liver dysfunction with total bilirubin > 3mg/dL.
5. Expected surgery lasting more than 6 hours or no extubation plan immediately after surgery.
6. Patients with < 45kg and > 100kg.
7. Pregnant or breastfeeding women.
8. History of hypersensitivity to any of the components of lidocaine or magnesium sulfate.
9. Patients who for some medical reason are contraindicated in the use of lidocaine or magnesium sulfate.
10. Patients who are taking analgesics (paracetamol or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs or opioids) in the 7 days prior to surgery.
11. History of alcohol or drug abuse or psychiatric illness.
12. History of Congestive Heart Failure or NYHA criteria III-IV or atrioventricular heart block.
13. Disease of the central nervous system.
14. Porphyria.
